The floor changes in this. She doesn't.

Different rooms, different jobs, different stretches I did not talk about out loud. Same small dog on the floor in the same 3 feet, chin down, waiting for me to be done with whatever it was.

She has been here for 10 of her 19 years. She was never impressed by any of it.

Nothing happens in this clip. She lies down. I keep going. That was the whole arrangement.

What keeps her comfortable now is written down. 13 pages, free, no clinic language.

Comment CESA and I'll send it to you.

https://consider-this.subscribepage.io

She is asleep in a shape that should not be comfortable.

Back legs straight out behind her, chin flat on the floor, one ear folded under itself. She is 19. She sleeps like this most afternoons now, and I stop for a 3 second stare every time. Not because anything is wrong. Because I want to be sure.

This is Cesa. I have had 10 of her 19 years.

People ask me what the secret is. There isn't one. It's small adjustments, made early and kept up. I wrote down the ones that actually made her more comfortable. 13 pages, plain words, comfort not medicine. Free.

Comment CESA and I'll send it to you.

My 19 year old just entered her party era and none of us were consulted about it.

Not me. Not the vet. Nobody got a vote.

She simply decided, and the rest of us are living here now.

She is 19 and she still works for it.

The green puzzle board goes down on the tile and she goes straight at it. Nose into one yellow square, then the next, then the white bone in the middle, working her way across the whole tray.

She does not rush it and she does not quit. That is pretty much her whole personality in 12 seconds.

Follow along for more of her. 🐾

Coming home after a long shift to something that does not care how the day went.

Not what got done. Not what didn't. Not the thing I said wrong at 10 AM and thought about until 6.

She just wants me back in the house. That is the entire review.

Comment CESA and I'll send you the Thursday note.

She gets up when she gets up. There is no negotiating it and I stopped trying around year 14.

I used to think slow mornings were something you earned. Turns out you just get a dog who refuses to hurry and eventually you learn.

POV, you peed in Mom's office.

But you are 19, you are adorable, and you are fully aware that 1 sad little face gets the whole case dismissed before it ever reaches trial.

I cleaned it up and then apologized to her. To HER. Sit with that.

She hears the car before the door.

By the time I am inside she is already up, and getting up takes her longer than it used to. Nails on the floor, no bark, just the walk toward me.

She has no idea how the shift went. She is not going to ask. She waited all day for this exact 4 seconds, and then she goes back to her spot.

She's 19. I have had 10 of those years.

If you have one of these at home and you're starting to notice the getting up taking longer, I wrote down what actually helped. 13 pages, plain words, comfort not medicine, free.

Comment CESA and I'll send it to you.

She checks the whole yard, patch by patch.

Pink harness, leash trailing out behind her, nose down in the grass. The dandelions are open. Half the yard is in sun and half is in shade and she walks through both.

Nothing really happens here. She goes slow, covers the ground she wants to cover, and at the end she stops where the grass runs out and looks straight up at me.
